title: NASA-based STATS thresholds
howToUse: Keys match the dashboard STATS ids and threshold names. Merge only critLo / warnLo / warnHi / critHi into STATS. A key that is missing here means the NASA data has no number for it (see gaps).
rule: Same as the dashboard zones: value <= critLo = crit; <= warnLo = warn; <= warnHi = ok; <= critHi = warn; above critHi = crit.
caveat: Demo use only. Earth clinical norms and NASA habitat limits as summarized in a compilation; not validated crew alert rules. Confirm the current NASA-STD-3001 revision before relying on them.

hr.label: Heart rate
hr.notes: Normal resting 60-100; flag when routinely below 60 or above 100 (p108). Above 140 bpm is the EVA performance-impairment marker (p106).
gaps: critLo: no NASA low heart-rate limit.
critHi 140 comes from EVA thermal context, not a resting limit.

spo2.label: SpO₂
spo2.notes: The compilation only says to record SpO₂ "if available".
gaps: No SpO₂ number anywhere in the NASA data. Keep the existing thresholds.

coreTemp.label: Core temp
coreTemp.notes: Clinical normal 36.5-37.3; fever above 38; hypothermia below 35.
gaps: In-flight core temp rose ~1 °C over ~75 days in one ISS study, so a healthy astronaut may read as caution.

resp.label: Breathing rate
resp.notes: Normal 12-18 at rest; raise if under 12 or over 25.
gaps: No NASA-specific respiratory standard; these are Earth clinical norms (the compilation says so).

bpSys.label: BP systolic
bpSys.notes: Under 120 normal; 130 or higher is high; 90 or lower is low if symptomatic.
gaps: critLo: no low-BP danger number.
Source lists hypertensive crisis as "diastolic above 90", flagged as an error and not used.

bpDia.label: BP diastolic
bpDia.notes: Under 80 normal; 80 or higher is high; 60 or lower is low if symptomatic. The source has no in-between band above 80, so 80+ goes straight to critical.
gaps: critLo: no low-BP danger number.

glucose.label: Glucose
glucose.notes: Fasting: normal 99 or below, prediabetes 100-125, diabetes 126+ (refer to flight surgeon). Under 70 is low; under 54 is the CGM level-2 low.
gaps: These are FASTING cutoffs. After meals healthy values exceed 99, so a 24 h trace will show caution often.
CGM targets are for people with diabetes; NIH gives none for healthy crew.

sleep.label: Sleep
sleep.notes: 7+ h (AASM), NASA standard 8 h opportunity. About a week at 5-6 h impaired performance; in-flight averages were 6-6.5 h.
gaps: Hours alone; NASA prefers measured sleep vs. opportunity, which the app does not separate.

exercise.label: Exercise
exercise.notes: ISS crews do about 1.25 h/day of actual exercise (2.5 h scheduled incl. changing and hygiene).
gaps: critLo: no NASA minimum below which exercise is "bad".
The tile goal of 2.5 h is scheduled time, not active exercise.

water.label: Water
water.notes: Related figures exist but none is a daily drinking target: 2.5-3 L/day is urine output, 240 mL/h is EVA-only, 15 mL/kg is pre-landing fluid loading.
gaps: No daily water-intake threshold in the NASA data. Keep the existing thresholds.

kcal.label: Energy intake
kcal.notes: Standard ISS menu is about 2,300-2,400 kcal/day; crews eating ~80% of need lost ~5% body mass.
gaps: critLo: NASA ties harm to 30 kcal per kg LEAN mass per day, which needs body composition the app does not have.
Individual requirement varies; core temp +1 °C adds ~350 kcal/day.

mood.label: Mood
mood.notes: The 1-5 scale is invented; NASA reports only the direction of stress across crews.
gaps: No mood threshold. Keep the existing thresholds.

cycleDay.label: Cycle day
cycleDay.notes: Compilation: no validated in-flight cycle prediction; label as background only.
gaps: No thresholds (none existed either).

bodyMass.label: Body mass
bodyMass.notes: Converted from % loss at a 73 kg baseline: 3.3% loss = 70.59 kg, 7.7% loss = 67.38 kg. Military data cited by NASA links 3.3-7.7% loss to performance decline, with large decline above 7.7%.
gaps: Military, not astronaut, data.
Values must be recalculated if the crew member's preflight mass is not 73 kg (use % of day-0 mass).

vision.label: Vision shift
vision.notes: SANS research definition: a refraction shift of 0.75 D or more from baseline.
gaps: Sign: the source describes a positive (hyperopic) shift; this keeps the dashboard's existing negative convention.
warnLo: no smaller "early" shift defined.

reaction.label: Reaction time
reaction.notes: The psychomotor vigilance task counts any single response over 500 ms as a lapse.
gaps: warnHi: no mean reaction-time cutoff in the data; 500 ms is a per-response lapse definition, so it is lenient for an average.

vo2.label: VO₂ max
vo2.notes: NASA-STD-3001 minimum preflight aerobic capacity is 32.9 mL/kg/min.
gaps: The report says 32.9 "may need careful review" for Moon/Mars.
warnLo: only a ±3% measurement-error band around preflight, not a caution level.

co2.label: Cabin CO₂
co2.notes: Under 2.5 mmHg (7-day average) keeps headache risk under 1%; the cabin limit is 3 mmHg (1 h average).
gaps: The app shows a daily snapshot, not the 1 h or 7-day averages the limits are written for.

cabinP.label: Cabin pressure
cabinP.notes: Allowed habitable total pressure 34.5-103 kPa (5.0-15.0 psia). ISS runs at 101.3.
gaps: No caution band: pressure only matters together with O₂, which cabinO2 below handles.

cabinO2.label: Cabin O₂
cabinO2.notes: Converted from inspired O₂ (PIO2) limits to the dashboard's dry ppO₂ at 101.3 kPa cabin pressure: PIO2 122 mmHg (absolute limit) = 17.34 kPa, normoxic 139-168 mmHg = 19.75-23.87 kPa, hyperoxia 333 mmHg = 47.3 kPa.
gaps: Conversion is only exact at 101.3 kPa; at other pressures recompute with dry = PIO2 x P/(P-47).
PIO2 under 127 mmHg also needs a health-monitoring plan; folded into caution here.
The ECLSS brief gives a narrower 145-155 mmHg target.

gravity.label: Gravity
gaps: No thresholds (none existed either).

lux.label: Light
lux.notes: Nominal 100-300 lux; 500 lux for reading; over 1,000 lux for high-precision work; 20 lux at night.
gaps: Right level depends on activity and time of day; no single upper limit.
NASA circadian lighting table (V2 8055) is not public.

pm25.label: Air particulate
pm25.notes: NASA respirable-dust limit is under 1 mg/m³ (= 1000 µg/m³).
gaps: NASA has no caution level, and its limit is far looser than Earth air-quality guidance (the old 15/35 values).

kpG.label: Geomagnetic
kpG.notes: The NASA data covers only the S (solar radiation) scale.
gaps: No G-scale thresholds. Keep the existing thresholds.

kpS.label: Solar radiation
kpS.notes: NOAA: S1-S2 have no effect on astronauts; S3 = radiation-hazard avoidance recommended on EVA; S4-S5 = unavoidable hazard on EVA. A storm starts at S1.

kpR.label: Radio blackout
kpR.notes: The NASA data covers only the S scale.
gaps: No R-scale thresholds. Keep the existing thresholds.

radiation.label: Career dose
radiation.notes: NASA career limit 600 mSv (waiver required at or above). 80% of the limit (480 mSv) as a planning warning.
gaps: The 480 mSv warning was suggested by the compilation author, not NASA.

noise.label: Noise
noise.notes: Normal ops: about 70 dBA averaged over 24 h. Any reading at or above 85 dBA is flagged.
gaps: The app value is a representative level, not a 24 h noise dose.

suitP.label: Suit pressure
suitP.notes: EMU nominal 4.3 psia (29.65 kPa); flag drift over 0.25 psi (1.72 kPa), i.e. outside 27.92-31.37 kPa.
gaps: Only valid for the 4.3 psia EMU; exploration suits run 3.8-8.2 psia.
No caution band, only the drift flag.

evaTime.label: Time remaining
evaTime.notes: EVA reports discuss consumable margins but give no remaining-time limit.
gaps: No thresholds in the data. Keep the existing thresholds.

suitO2.label: Suit O₂
suitO2.notes: Apollo context only: 6 EVAs ended with under 10% usable O₂, cited as thin margins, not a limit.
gaps: No suit O₂ threshold. Keep the existing thresholds.

helmetCo2.label: Helmet CO₂
helmetCo2.notes: Suit inlet under 2 mmHg; suit nominal 3-15 mmHg; contingency limit 20 mmHg inspired for up to 1 h.
gaps: Treats anything past the 15 mmHg nominal ceiling as critical; 20 mmHg is the absolute contingency cap.

metabolic.label: Metabolic rate
metabolic.notes: Flag against the 2,000 BTU/h suit cooling limit (= 2110 kJ/h). Apollo EVA rates were 780-1,200 BTU/h (823-1266 kJ/h).
gaps: warnHi: no caution level; only the cooling limit.
